How to read this catalog Each feature is one file, written against the template below. Fields may not be omitted, but may be *empty by declaration* — see the field contracts. ### 1.1 Entry template 1. **Name and Classification** — feature name + tier (**Frozen 4.0** / **Experimental** / **Deferred** / **Rejected–Superseded** / **Rejected–Never Existed**), the spec section, and the REQ slice/PR that landed it (traceability — every entry links back to its delivery). 2. **Intent** — one paragraph: what the construct does. 3. **Also Known As** — spec PR/issue numbers and former names. The 4.x drafts rename things; this field is the antidote. 4. **History / Supersedes** — which 1.x–3.x idiom this replaces, with a migration pair. If the feature is genuinely new, declare: *"None — new capability; 3.1 workaround: …"* — emptiness must be informative, not accidental. 5. **Motivation** — the problem in 4.x terms: why the pre-existing idioms were not enough. 6. **Language Alignment** — prior art in other languages (F#, Haskell, JS, Python…), **including semantic-drift warnings** where XPath deliberately differs from the language it borrowed from (argument position, null-vs-empty, renames). 7. **Applicability** — when to use it; when *not* (library code targeting 3.1, hot paths, …). 8. **Structure** — the grammar fragment or syntax shape. 9. **Participants** — how Bosak models it: parser flag, AST node(s), opcodes, version-gate entry. 10. **Collaborations** — interactions with other features (e.g., destructuring × typed-let coercion × lexical scoping). 11. **Consequences** — benefits *and* liabilities, including any deliberate breaking change. 12. **Implementation** — files, versions, and where the version gate rejects (XPST0003 at 3.1, XPST0017, …). 13. **Sample Code** — a worked real-world case with input, complete code, required context, expected output, compatibility level, and a meaningful edge case; syntax probes supplement the case and cover each form. 14. **Performance Notes** — cost class (zero-cost desugar / small constant overhead / hot-path relevant), plus measured deltas **only** when they carry revision + date from `benchmarks/Bosak.Benchmarks` (BenchmarkDotNet). Ad-hoc timings do not belong here; the harness owns numbers. 15. **Known Uses** — the qt4tests sets that pin the behavior and their gate status. 16. **Related Features** — cross-links to other catalog entries. For book-style reading, begin with Intent, Motivation, Applicability, and Sample Code, then use History, Consequences, and Related Features to evaluate alternatives. Participants, Collaborations, and Implementation provide a separate contributor reference. Authors should open with a practical scenario and link its runnable case before presenting engine details. fn:scan

Catalog entry — Functions · Experimental

## 1. Name and Classification **`fn:scan`** — **Experimental** (ships only at the `XPath40Experimental` level; static XPST0017 at both `XPath31` *and* frozen `XPath40`). Spec: F&O 4.0 §2.5.15, added by qt4cg Issue 2823 / PR 2824 (31 July 2026). Landed: REQ-123 S1 (1.1.0 track), level-plumbing slice 2026-10-09. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [F&O 4.0: fn:scan](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-scan). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. Draft evolution: [QT4CG PR #2824](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/pull/2824) records the scan proposal referenced by the adoption dossier. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #98](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/98), [immutable mainline revision `bd18e42f`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/bd18e42f33b5e69817f059f6429f4b08e639a5a3) (2026-10-09). This identifies the engine delivery; later documentation examples do not redefine that delivery. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent Return every intermediate accumulator of a left fold as a **sequence of single-member arrays**: `fn:scan($input, $init, $action)` yields `[$init]`, then `[$action($acc, $item, $pos)]` for each input item — N input items produce N+1 arrays. There is no additional outer array. ## 3. Also Known As "Prefix scan", "running fold". **Do not implement** `scan-left` / `scan-right`: those names never existed in the accepted draft — the pair was consolidated into the single left-fold `fn:scan` before stabilization (see [mapping-arrow-gtgt.md](../rejected/mapping-arrow-gtgt.md) for the sibling rename story). ## 4. History / Supersedes Supersedes hand-threaded accumulation of intermediate states in 3.1. The [complete stock-ledger baseline](../examples/fn-scan/before.xpath) uses `fold-left` and `array:append`; the [experimental case](../examples/fn-scan/main.xpath) uses `fn:scan`. Both display `100,120,85,95` for an opening stock of 100 units and movements of +20, -35, and +10. | Before (3.1) | After (4.0-Exp) | |---|---| | `fold-left($movements, [100], function($states, $delta) { array:append($states, $states(array:size($states)) + $delta) })` | `fn:scan($movements, 100, function($balance, $delta) { $balance + $delta })` | ## 5. Motivation Fold returns its final accumulator; stock ledgers and running totals need every intermediate state. A 3.1 fold must explicitly retain that history. Scan expresses the history requirement directly and includes the initial state for comparison. ## 6. Language Alignment Direct prior art: Haskell `scanl`, Clojure `reductions`, F# `Seq.scan`, Kotlin `runningFold`. Drift warning: XPath returns a **sequence of single-member arrays**, allowing each accumulator to hold a sequence without flattening it into the other states. Arity-2 callbacks receive accumulator and item only; the runtime can supply position to an arity-3 callback. ## 7. Applicability Use for: running aggregations, incremental derivations, anything where each input item emits a new accumulator state. Do **not** use for: anything that must compile at frozen `XPath40` or 3.1 (static XPST0017); final-state-only folds (`fn:fold-left` is clearer and one array shorter); unstable-surface intolerance — this function postdates the June-2026 churn line and its exact shape may still move. ## 8. Structure ``` fn:scan(input as item()*, init as item()*, action as fn(*)) as array(*)* ``` ## 9. Participants - `FunctionLibrary` — experimental-only signature template (`IsXPath40ExperimentalOnly`), invisible to `fn:function-lookup` / dynamic dispatch below the experimental level. - `EvaluationContext.IsXPath40Experimental` — runtime level flag. - Version gate (`XPath31Expression`) — static XPST0017 in call form *and* named-function-ref form at both lower levels. ## 10. Collaborations - The **experimental level plumbing** (REQ-123 S1) is the collaboration that matters: `fn:scan` was the first function gated exclusively to `XPath40Experimental`, and it established the template every later experimental addition follows (dedicated signature templates, lookup invisibility, call+ref static errors). - Destructuring `let` ([destructuring-let.md](../operators-and-syntax/destructuring-let.md)) is the natural consumer of each emitted single-member array's shape in surrounding code. ## 11. Consequences Benefits: direct expression of all intermediate states; the callback position parameter enables position-aware accumulations. Retaining the history requires storage for its states; no constant-memory guarantee is implied. Liabilities: **experimental-tier semantics may change as the draft moves** — the N+1 / single-member-array shape is precisely the kind of detail a WG review adjusts. Pin your usage to a Bosak version and re-run the qt4tests `fn-scan` set (if promoted by then) on upgrades. ## 12. Implementation **C04 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Expression/call/focus reconciliation](../EXPRESSION-CALL-FOCUS-RECONCILIATION.md) covers REQ123-scan. scan is Experimental-only in calls and lookup, with N+1 single-member-array states and empty input retaining the seed. Its existing gate retry is not frozen API promotion. No new function syntax or frozen promotion. C02 callback semantics and C06 host/profile ownership remain distinct from membership in GatedSets. This is bounded production/profile evidence, not full grammar or AC-04 acceptance. **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles N+1 accumulator states retain single-member array boundaries; Empty input retains the initial state; Position-aware callback; Experimental-only availability. **Boundaries:** No frozen-profile adoption or constant-memory guarantee; generic function coercion beyond verified callbacks is not certified. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Files: `src/Bosak.XPath.Standard/Functions/FunctionLibrary.cs` (experimental signature + implementation), `src/Bosak.XPath.Api/XPath31Expression.cs` (experimental-aware static gate), `src/Bosak.XPath.Runtime/Vm/EvaluationContext.cs` (`IsXPath40Experimental`). Version gate: XPST0017 at `XPath31` **and** `XPath40`; legal only at `XPath40Experimental`. Unit evidence: experimental-level tests in `Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests` (see REQ-123 S1). ## 13. Sample Code Practical case: [stock ledger](../examples/fn-scan/main.xpath). The [empty-movement case](../examples/fn-scan/edge.xpath) returns only the opening balance, displayed as `100`. Both cases require `XPath40Experimental`; the [earlier baseline](../examples/fn-scan/before.xpath) runs at `XPath31`. ~~~xquery fn:scan((1, 2, 3), 0, fn($acc, $it) { $acc + $it }) (: → [0], [1], [3], [6] — every running total, init first :) fn:scan((), "start", fn($acc, $it) { $acc || $it }) (: → ["start"] — empty input yields just the init :) ~~~ ## 14. Performance Notes Implementation expectation: one callback per input item and one wrapper array per retained state. Accumulator size can dominate storage and callback cost. No measured comparison against the 3.1 array-append baseline is claimed. ## 15. Known Uses Published examples: `fn-scan-main`, `fn-scan-edge`, `fn-scan-before` in `CatalogExampleTests`. The successful experimental cases also verify refusal at both lower compatibility levels. This is example evidence, separate from gate status. qt4tests set `fn-scan` is promoted into `GatedSets` in [ConformanceRunner40](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs). The 1.1.0 gate run records 11 experimental-level passes and zero gated failures. Gate membership does not move the function into the frozen compatibility tier; its successful examples still require `XPath40Experimental`. **Named implementation evidence:** [`Evaluate_Scan_XPath40Experimental_Works`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). Named promoted sets: `fn-scan`. These references describe existing evidence; this documentation update does not rerun or promote the full conformance suite. ## 16. Related Features - [mapping-arrow-gtgt.md](../rejected/mapping-arrow-gtgt.md) — the sibling "consolidated/renamed before stabilization" story. - [destructuring-let.md](../operators-and-syntax/destructuring-let.md) — frozen-tier contrast from the same delivery wave. - [method-call-operator.md](../operators-and-syntax/method-call-operator.md) — another post-June-2026 deferred surface. *Entry created 2026-10-10 (REQ-126 scaffold).*

xslt-instructions/module-profiles.md.text:
Module and used-package profile propagation

Bosak host policy - bounded executable reference

**Public 1.23.8 - 23 October 2026:** The function default-mode fix and host/module profile coverage are [published and verified](../../RELEASE-1.23.8-PUBLICATION.md). Current catalog:76 entries/3,073 documentation checks. REQ-126/AC-03 remain partial; Braid smoke/acceptance is separate. Earlier source/unpublished/PR checkpoints below are historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Module/profile propagation** - implemented Bosak host composition, with an opt-in experimental XSLT draft profile and frozen embedded XPath 4.0. The same compilation host applies to a directly included, imported or used-package module, while expression selection and forwards-compatible validation retain the dependency's own effective version. This is not a new grammar feature or an experimental XPath promotion. Profile implementation: [cc07d50f8a55bdca907d398d4916d95cbed36734](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/cc07d50f8a55bdca907d398d4916d95cbed36734). This slice depends on the separate [function default-mode fix](../../XSLT-FUNCTION-DEFAULT-MODE.md), [PR416](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/416), source 1.23.8 unpublished; public 1.23.7 is unchanged. Current comparison: [immutable XSLT XML](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/b4723ff52fd9d4fabf2b4cd33bd44f21939c512c/specifications/xslt-40/src/xslt.xml), include/import/use-package/backwards/forwards/modes sections, refreshed on 23 October 2026. This is not recovered historical adoption. [Audit](../MODULE-PROFILE-BOUNDARIES.md). ## 2. Intent Move a transformation function into a dependency without losing the selected compiler host or silently replacing the dependency's declared version with the principal stylesheet's version. ## 3. Also Known As Include/import module loading and used-package compilation. An XSLT package name/package-version here identifies an XML library package; it is distinct from the Bosak NuGet release version. Include, import and use-package are different composition mechanisms, not interchangeable aliases. ## 4. History / Supersedes Each relation has a baseline library at version 3.0 using explicit if/then/else and a version 4.0 library using otherwise. The principal report remains version 3.0 and calls the same quantity function. The six complete report/library pairs in [the task](../examples/module-profiles/README.md) run under both hosts. This is Bosak compatibility policy, not a promise that an arbitrary XSLT 3.0 processor can run a 4.0 library. ## 5. Motivation A shared order-quantity function defaults a missing quantity to1 while retaining explicit zero. It can be maintained in one dependency rather than duplicated in a principal template. The examples separate library migration from the principal version and verify namespace, URI and registration setup together with the actual report. ## 6. Language Alignment The current XSLT draft gives included/imported modules and packages their own declaration/static-context rules. Bosak propagates the selected processor host through compilation; it does not overwrite the child version. Legacy's hybrid policy selects embedded XPath by effective version, whereas Xslt40Draft supplies frozen 4.0 even in a 3.0 library. The tests use nonconflicting function names to isolate that policy. They do not establish import precedence, override/accept/expose semantics, or general equivalence between composition mechanisms. ## 7. Applicability Use this reference for one direct include/import edge or one registered used package loaded from local files, compiled with either public host profile. Multi-hop graphs, package version ranges, overrides, schema/static parameters, dynamic evaluate, authoring, streaming, remote/resource-policy behavior and complete default-mode propagation are outside this slice. ## 8. Structure | Dependency effective version | Legacy host | Draft host | |---|---|---| |3.0 | The supplied otherwise expression refuses XPST0003, regardless of principal 3.0/4.0 | Frozen4.0 expression succeeds | |4.0 | Frozen4.0 expression succeeds, even with a 3.0 principal | Frozen4.0 expression succeeds | | Module3.0 with local function4.0 | Local override enables the supplied 4.0 expression | Remains frozen 4.0 | | Module4.0 with local function3.0 | Local override refuses the supplied 4.0 expression | Remains frozen 4.0 | The selected host's forwards-compatible ceiling still applies to the child's effective version:3.0 for Legacy and4.0 for Draft. A future-version principal does not make a known-version child forwards compatible in Draft. scan remains unavailable under both hosts in the supplied 4.0 libraries. ## 9. Participants [XsltCompiler](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Api/XsltCompiler.cs) captures ProcessorProfile and the URI resolver. [Stylesheet](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Stylesheet/Stylesheet.cs) resolves includes, imports and used packages. [XsltFunctionLibrary.RegisterPackage](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Api/XsltFunctionLibrary.cs) maps a package name/version to an absolute module URI. The [catalog runner](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) supplies optional per-case package registrations and always cleans them in finally; its existing package-registry collection serializes these tests with other registry users. ## 10. Collaborations An app/main.xsl principal resolves ../library/module.xsl relative to its own file URI for include/import. A package principal uses a synthetic URN and exact package-version 1.0, registered to the corresponding absolute XML file URI before compilation. The library declares p:quantity and its own version. The principal passes each line node, preserves order and sums the returned quantities. Registry setup is caller/test setup; the XML file does not embed a compiler profile. ## 11. Consequences Changing the principal's version alone does not promote a 3.0 dependency in Legacy. A4.0 dependency does not promote unrelated principal expressions either; this entry tests calls into the library, not every caller expression. Unknown attributes on the supplied apply-templates instruction follow the child/local version and inherited host. Those validation probes exposed an independent function default-mode bug: legal success cases raised XTSE0020 after validation. The separate fix preserves their expected results rather than recording the bug as supported behavior. ## 12. Implementation The 114 cases are 66 focused host/version/static/validation/refusal controls and 48 complete report runs. Before package setup the baseline was70pass/44fail:38 missing-registration failures and six default-mode failures. Scoped registrations changed this to105pass/9fail, revealing the same runtime issue in packages too. On the isolated fix all 114 pass with unchanged expected results. The runner adds optional packages metadata and cleanup on both success and failure; rows without it preserve their prior setup. [Machine audit](../MODULE-PROFILE-BOUNDARIES.json). ## 13. Sample Code For each relation, [the complete task](../examples/module-profiles/README.md) links the baseline and mixed-version principal/library files. With [normal.xml](../examples/module-profiles/normal.xml), both variants under both hosts emit `A=2|B=1|C=0|lines=3;total=3`. Empty input emits `lines=0;total=0`; reordered input changes line order; invalid integer text raises FORG0001. All namespaces, fixtures, dependency locations, package registrations and expected results are supplied. The library expression `(xs:integer($line/@qty) ?? 1)` is actually executed in the4.0 variants. ## 14. Performance Notes These examples verify compilation policy and module loading, not a performance optimization. Each run compiles real local files and may allocate a separate package/module context. No compile-cache, concurrency or timing benefit is claimed. Reusing a compiled executable or resolving larger graphs needs separate measurements and contracts. ## 15. Known Uses Applicable AC-03 evidence: `module-profile-include-root4-module3-legacy`, `module-profile-import-root3-module4-legacy`, `module-profile-package-root4-module3-draft40`, `module-profile-package-root4-module4-local3-legacy`, `module-profile-import-validation-root5-module4-draft40`, `module-profile-package-static-root4-module3-draft40` and `module-profile-package-report-module40-normal-legacy`, plus all 114 cases listed in [the audit](../MODULE-PROFILE-BOUNDARIES.json) and [manifest](../examples/cases.json). Named [ProcessorProfileTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/ProcessorProfileTests.cs) methods ModulesInheritProfile, ModuleValidationInheritsProfile and UsedPackageInheritsProfile provide independent API evidence. This XSLT host/module contract has no applicable XPath-only gate assignment; no gate is invented or promoted. ## 16. Related Features [Ordinary stylesheet profiles](processor-profiles.md), [otherwise](../operators-and-syntax/otherwise-operator.md), [function default-mode correction](../../XSLT-FUNCTION-DEFAULT-MODE.md) and [coverage reconciliation](../COVERAGE-RECONCILIATION.md). General package visibility/version resolution, transitive graphs and full lexical default-mode contexts remain follow-ups. REQ-126 and D2/D3/D4/AC03 remain partial.

xslt-instructions/processor-profiles.md.text:
Stylesheet versions and processor profiles

Bosak host policy - bounded executable reference

## 1. Name and Classification **Version/profile boundary** - implemented Bosak host policy. Legacy is the default compatibility profile; Xslt40Draft is an opt-in experimental XSLT processor profile whose embedded XPath is frozen 4.0. This is not a new language feature or a promotion to XPath40Experimental. Public/source 1.23.7 already provides this API. Original profile delivery: [cc07d50f8a55bdca907d398d4916d95cbed36734](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/cc07d50f8a55bdca907d398d4916d95cbed36734). Current comparison: [immutable XSLT XML](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/b4723ff52fd9d4fabf2b4cd33bd44f21939c512c/specifications/xslt-40/src/xslt.xml), sections backwards, backwards-3.0, forwards and standard-attributes, refreshed against upstream master on 23 October 2026. This comparison pin does not recover a historical adopted specification revision. [Delivery audit](../HOST-PROFILE-BOUNDARIES.md). ## 2. Intent Choose an execution host explicitly and understand how a local version declaration affects XPath syntax and forwards-compatible validation within that host. ## 3. Also Known As Processor capability/profile, effective stylesheet version, embedded XPath compatibility and forwards-compatible ceiling are separate concepts. XsltProcessorProfile.Xslt40Draft and XPathCompatibility.XPath40Experimental are different API settings; the former does not enable experimental XPath functions. ## 4. History / Supersedes The [baseline report](../examples/host-profiles/report-baseline.xsl) uses ordinary 3.0 expressions. The [mixed-version report](../examples/host-profiles/report-local40.xsl) keeps a 3.0 root but places version 4.0 on its template and uses the otherwise operator. Both are executed under both Bosak hosts. A local 4.0 block is not a portable way to give an arbitrary XSLT 3.0 processor XPath 4.0 capability; these are Bosak host contracts. ## 5. Motivation An order report defaults an absent quantity to1 while preserving an explicit zero. Migrating one template allows a compact otherwise expression without changing the root version. A caller still needs to know whether its host treats a lower local version as a syntax boundary. [The complete task](../examples/host-profiles/README.md) gives input, all instructions, exact results and malformed-data behavior. ## 6. Language Alignment The pinned XSLT 4.0 draft defines effective version from the nearest applicable [xsl:]version attribute, with special rules including xsl:output. It defines no 3.0-versus4.0 compatibility-mode differences for a 4.0 processor. The draft profile's acceptance of frozen 4.0 XPath within version 3.0 is therefore intentional. Bosak Legacy is its preserved compatibility policy, not an assertion that it exactly emulates every W3C3.0 processor: it uses a 3.0 forwards-compatible ceiling while selecting embedded XPath 4.0 at effective versions at least 4.0. ## 7. Applicability Use this entry when compiling an ordinary stylesheet with XsltCompiler or generating a locally versioned block. This slice excludes includes/imports, used packages, schema/static parameters, authoring/edit APIs, dynamic evaluate, streaming, detailed fallback behavior and versions1.0/2.0. Existing tests elsewhere may cover some of those paths; this entry does not claim their full matrix. ## 8. Structure | Host | Embedded XPath in the supplied ordinary expression paths | Forwards-compatible ceiling | |---|---|---| | Legacy (default) | Effective version below 4.0 selects XPath 3.1; at least 4.0 selects frozen 4.0 |3.0 | | Xslt40Draft (explicit opt-in) | Frozen4.0 independently of local 3.0/4.0 version |4.0 | A non-root XSLT instruction uses unqualified version; a literal result element uses xsl:version. The nearest declaration wins. xsl:output/@version selects serialization behavior and does not promote the surrounding stylesheet's XPath level. The ceiling describes capability-sensitive forwards compatibility; it does not enable arbitrary future syntax. ## 9. Participants [XsltCompiler.ProcessorProfile](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Api/XsltCompiler.cs) selects the public host enum [XsltProcessorProfile](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Api/XsltProcessorProfile.cs). [Stylesheet](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Stylesheet/Stylesheet.cs) resolves GetEffectiveVersion, GetXPathCompatibility and IsForwardsCompatibleElement. The [catalog runner](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) supplies the explicitly requested host to the public compiler, retaining Legacy as the default for all older rows. ## 10. Collaborations In the mixed-version report, the root 3.0 declaration remains outside the locally4.0 template. The template's selection, per-line expression and total inherit4.0 in Legacy. Draft supplies frozen 4.0 throughout either stylesheet. Static use-when, shadow-produced select expressions, AVTs and ordinary select expressions have separate focused controls; changing a serializer version is not a shortcut for changing their host. ## 11. Consequences A Legacy 4.0 stylesheet with a local 3.0 instruction refuses 0x10 with XPST0003; Draft accepts it. A3.0 Legacy root with a local 4.0 template accepts it. Under Draft, an unknown unqualified apply-templates attribute at effective4.0 raises XTSE0090; above 4.0 it is ignored. Legacy's tested apply-templates path ignores it above 3.0. These are bounded instruction controls, not a certification of every unknown attribute/instruction. scan remains unavailable with XPST0017 under both XSLT hosts, including Draft. Runtime malformed quantities still raise FORG0001. ## 12. Implementation Fifty focused host/version cases plus sixteen full report runs execute66 manifest cases through the public compiler. The initial runner forced Legacy and produced56 passes/10 failures against rows requesting Draft. Those failures are retained as a runner limitation, not an engine defect. The runner now accepts explicit processorProfile values legacy/draft40 and rejects unknown spellings; omitted values preserve Legacy. Existing manifest rows and outcomes are unchanged. No engine, public API, version, gate or release changes. [Machine audit](../HOST-PROFILE-BOUNDARIES.json). ## 13. Sample Code The actual [mixed-version stylesheet](../examples/host-profiles/report-local40.xsl) declares version 3.0 on xsl:stylesheet and version 4.0 on xsl:template. Its quantity expression is `(xs:integer(@qty) ?? 1)`. With [normal.xml](../examples/host-profiles/normal.xml), both profiles produce `A=2|B=1|C=0|lines=3;total=3`, exactly matching the baseline. Empty input yields `lines=0;total=0`; reordered rows change line order; `qty="oops"` raises FORG0001. [Task and fixtures](../examples/host-profiles/README.md) include full context and all outcomes. Host configuration is the public ProcessorProfile property; each manifest row states it explicitly. ## 14. Performance Notes Host/version selection is compilation policy, not a performance optimization. Both reports parse and sum quantities per reading; no timing/allocation comparison is claimed. Compilation captures the profile; existing named tests separately verify behavior when a compiler is reused. ## 15. Known Uses Applicable AC-03 evidence: `host-profile-select-root3-legacy`, `host-profile-select-root3-draft40`, `host-profile-select-root4-local3-draft40`, `host-profile-ancestor-root3-wrapper4-local3-legacy`, `host-profile-avt-root3-draft40`, `host-profile-use-when-root3-draft40`, `host-profile-future-attribute-root4-draft40`, `host-profile-report-local40-normal-legacy` and all other cases in [the audit](../HOST-PROFILE-BOUNDARIES.json) and [manifest](../examples/cases.json), run by CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome. This host/compiler/XSLT contract has no applicable XPath-only gate assignment. Named [ProcessorProfileTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/ProcessorProfileTests.cs): DraftXPathIndependentOfVersion, LocalVersion, StaticXPathProfile, UnknownAttributeMatrix, CompilationCapturesProfile and DefaultAndInvalidProfile provide independent public-API evidence. The shadow controls generate a 4.0 select expression from a string-valued shadow attribute; they do not certify every4.0 form inside the shadow expression itself. No gate is invented or promoted. ## 16. Related Features [Numeric literals](../operators-and-syntax/numeric-literals.md), [otherwise](../operators-and-syntax/otherwise-operator.md), [xsl:select](xsl-select.md) and [coverage reconciliation](../COVERAGE-RECONCILIATION.md). Package/import propagation is a subsequent bounded slice, not implied acceptance from this entry. REQ-126 and D2/D3/D4/AC-03 remain partial.
